correctness.rationale: For every \(d\ge2\), full-dimensional compact convex \(K\) whose normalized depth is maximized at \(0\), and \(0<r\le1\) with \(-rK\subseteq K\), every ambient halfspace through \((1,0)\) contains at least \(\delta(K)|K|\) in its middle section. Its excluded bottom mass reflects injectively into the included top section, forcing at least \(r^d|K|\) outer mass. Horizontal sections satisfy the bound separately. Sufficiently steep halfspaces bound the depth above by \((r^d+\delta(K))|K|\) in the middle, by \(\delta(K)|K|\) on top, and by \(r^d|K|\) on the bottom. Thus the exact maximum fraction is \((\delta(K)+r^d)/(2+r^d)\). The sharp Grünbaum centroid bound plus facet cap gives \(\delta(\Delta)=(d/(d+1))^d\) for a simplex, and barycentric reflection gives \(-r\Delta\subseteq\Delta\iff r\le1/d\). The parameter conversion \(\varepsilon=r^d/(2+r^d)\) yields the exact planar value \(2/9+7\varepsilon/9\) for \(0<\varepsilon\le1/9\). The actual independent program replay gave `VERIFY_OK 5390 exact-rational assertions`; these finite checks supplement the universal analytic argument.

value.rationale: The sharpness configuration in arXiv:2609.32953v1 was quantified by a one-sided finite-mass estimate and its limit \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\); the exact value for \(0<\varepsilon\le1/9\) is a natural missing invariant. Reflection pairing extends that motivated planar calculation into a structural theorem for any convex body about any Tukey-depth maximizer in every \(d\ge2\), for a nonzero interval of radii. The simplex reflection threshold \(r=1/d\) is a meaningful geometric boundary, not an arbitrary cutoff. The result does not claim to solve general mixed-integer centerpoint theory.
